question.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form ${P}_{n}(t)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{t}^{3}-10{t}^{2}+10t & =-14t-2{t}^{2} \\ -2{t}^{3}-8{t}^{2}+10t & =-14t \\ -2{t}^{3}-8{t}^{2}+24t & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $-2t.$ We can factor out the $-2t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{t}^{3}-8{t}^{2}+24t & =0 \\ -2t({t}^{2}+4t-12) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression ${t}^{2}+4t-12$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2t({t}^{2}+4t-12) & =0 \\ -2t(t+6)(t-2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $t=0,$ $t=-6,$ and $t=2.$
